methods.label: Work backward
methods.explanation:
Undo the mistaken operations in reverse order to recover the starting number. Before Pat subtracted \(14\), the value was \(16+14=30\). Since this was the result of dividing the starting number by \(6\), the starting number was \(30\cdot6=180\).

Using the intended operations gives
\[
180\cdot6+14=1080+14=1094.
\]
This is greater than \(1000\), so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: Reversing two arithmetic operations and evaluating the intended calculation require only elementary arithmetic.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central target is recovering an unknown starting value through inverse relationships among arithmetic operations. Integer mixed-operation calculation supports the recovery and the final evaluation.
